title: Warn on constraints whose globs match zero files (dead constraint detection)
description:
A constraint whose from/to/scope glob matches zero indexed files enforces nothing but reads as protection — false confidence. This becomes acute with PRD-seeded rules.toml (vidhi-sutra-seed, see vidhi project) where globs are written before or during scaffolding and a path rename silently kills the rule. Analogous to existing alias orphan detection.

Surface it in sutra_constraints(action="list") output (e.g. matched_file_count per constraint, warning when 0) and as a finding in sutra_review. Zero matches on `to` of a forbidden_dep may be legitimate (the target was deleted — rule is vestigial); zero on `from` means the rule guards nothing. Either way the human should see it.

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review (bb2f504..30331bd):

Verdict: needs-attention

[medium] Boundary coverage falsely flags component-id rules as dead (src/constraints/mod.rs:150-156)
constraint_coverage checks boundary references only against component names. The resolver accepts both component names and component ids, so a valid boundary rule written with stable component ids will get zero coverage and appear as a dead_constraint warning/finding in list and review output. That can push users to remove valid protection.
Recommendation: Pass both component ids and names into constraint_coverage and use the same name-or-id matching semantics as boundary resolution. Add a unit test where from_component/to_component are component ids.
